--- title: 'Chapter 8: Panel Data' jupyter: mixtape-causalpy --- ## Causal Inference: The Mixtape → CausalPy **Mixtape chapter**: [Panel Data](https://mixtape-1ed.netlify.app/08-panel_data) **CausalPy method**: `PanelRegression` --- ### Overview Pooled OLS treats every client session as a separate draw. If providers who take riskier sessions also differ in ways that do not change across their sessions — and those differences affect price — the provider effect sits in the error and the slopes are biased. The within estimator, which is what provider fixed effects estimate, subtracts each provider's mean. That deletes the time-invariant unit effect \(u_i\). A slope is then identified only from within-provider variation. Two conditions have to hold: the idiosyncratic error is strictly exogenous given the unit effect, and the regressor actually moves inside the provider. A covariate that is constant for each provider is wiped, not estimated. ::: {.callout-important} Fixed effects are not a fix for reverse causality, and they are not a fix for a confounder that changes across sessions. The chapter shows those failures with published tables from @cornwell1994 and @cornwell1997. Those datasets are not in the Mixtape repo. This page cites the tables and does not recreate them. ::: The coded exercise is Cunningham and Kendall's Survey of Adult Service Providers. Each row is one of a provider's recent client sessions, not a calendar year. The outcome is log hourly price (`lnw`). [Table 8.3](https://mixtape-1ed.netlify.app/08-panel_data) reports three columns on the same balanced sample: pooled OLS, provider fixed effects, and OLS on provider-demeaned variables. Columns 2 and 3 are the same point estimates. This page does not refit those columns. It estimates the within relationship with one Bayesian demeaned regression and compares the posterior means to the published fixed-effects point estimates. The book does not put session fixed effects in this regression. ### What we'll cover 1. Clean the panel to the book's 1,028-row sample 2. Show which covariates the within transformation wipes 3. One Bayesian within regression, compared with Table 8.3's published point estimates, and why its interval is not the book's clustered standard error ### Mixtape files implemented | File | Description | Status | |------|-------------|--------| | `sasp.py` | Sex-worker panel, pooled OLS versus provider FE | 🟡 Bayesian within means versus Table 8.3; clustered SEs not estimated | `bail.py` is a judge-leniency instrumental-variables design, not this page. The cluster-robust Monte Carlos (`cluster1.py`–`cluster4.py`) are not in this chapter, and CausalPy does not report cluster-robust frequentist standard errors. Neither is estimated here. ## Setup ::: {#96b1a574 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import warnings warnings.filterwarnings("ignore") import numpy as np import pandas as pd import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import arviz as az import causalpy as cp import sys sys.path.insert(0, "../src") from mixtape_causalpy import load_sasp %matplotlib inline ``` ::: The outcome is `lnw`. The regressors are the full Table 8.3 list, not a shortened covariate set. Provider characteristics before `age_cl` do not vary across a provider's sessions. Client and session characteristics from `age_cl` onward do. ::: {#67fbb21c .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} TIME_INVARIANT = [ "age", "asq", "bmi", "hispanic", "black", "other", "asian", "schooling", "cohab", "married", "divorced", "separated", ] TIME_VARYING = [ "age_cl", "unsafe", "llength", "reg", "asq_cl", "appearance_cl", "provider_second", "asian_cl", "black_cl", "hispanic_cl", "othrace_cl", "hot", "massage_cl", ] FORMULA_VARS = ["lnw", *TIME_INVARIANT, *TIME_VARYING] # Book order, from python/sasp.py. Table 8.3 citations below use this list. REGRESSORS = TIME_INVARIANT + TIME_VARYING # Table 8.3 point estimates at the printed precision. Parentheses in the book # are provider-clustered standard errors; those are not targets. BOOK = { "unsafe": (0.013, 0.051), "llength": (-0.308, -0.435), "reg": (-0.047, -0.037), "appearance_cl": (0.020, 0.006), "provider_second": (0.055, 0.113), "othrace_cl": (0.156, 0.142), "hot": (0.133, 0.052), "massage_cl": (-0.134, -0.001), } DISCUSSED = [ "unsafe", "llength", "reg", "appearance_cl", "provider_second", "hot", "massage_cl", ] ``` ::: ## Load and clean `provider_second` is not numeric in the Stata file. `pd.read_stata` brings it in as a labelled category (`"1. No"`, `"2. Yes"`). Check that before fitting. The other regressors are numeric. ::: {#4aad8ffb .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} raw = load_sasp() print(f"Raw shape: {raw.shape}") print("Non-numeric columns:") print(raw.select_dtypes(exclude="number").dtypes) print(raw["provider_second"].value_counts(dropna=False)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Raw shape: (1787, 31) Non-numeric columns: provider_second category dtype: object provider_second 1. No 1630 2. Yes 87 NaN 70 Name: count, dtype: int64 ``` ::: ::: Cleaning follows the chapter [@cunningham2021], not a looser `dropna` on the whole frame: 1. Drop a row if any Table 8.3 variable is missing. 2. Keep providers who still have all four sessions. 3. Recode `provider_second` to 1/0, matching `sasp.py` (`"2. Yes"` → 1). The cleaned frame has to be 1,028 rows. A different sample is not comparable to Table 8.3. ::: {#b77cc1f2 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} missing = [column for column in ["id", "session", *FORMULA_VARS] if column not in raw.columns] if missing: raise RuntimeError(f"sasp_panel.dta is missing {missing}") sasp = raw.dropna(subset=FORMULA_VARS).copy() sessions_left = sasp.groupby("id")["session"].transform("size") sasp = sasp.loc[sessions_left == 4].copy() labels = set(sasp["provider_second"].astype(str).unique()) if labels != {"1. No", "2. Yes"}: raise RuntimeError(f"unexpected provider_second labels: {sorted(labels)}") sasp["provider_second"] = np.where( sasp["provider_second"].astype(str) == "2. Yes", 1.0, 0.0 ) if len(sasp) != 1028: raise RuntimeError(f"cleaned SASP sample has {len(sasp)} rows, expected 1028") if not (sasp.groupby("id").size() == 4).all(): raise RuntimeError("cleaned sample is not balanced at four sessions") print(f"Cleaned rows: {len(sasp)}") print(f"Providers: {sasp['id'].nunique()}") print(f"Sessions per provider: {sorted(int(n) for n in sasp.groupby('id').size().unique())}") print(sasp["provider_second"].value_counts().rename("provider_second")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Cleaned rows: 1028 Providers: 257 Sessions per provider: [4] provider_second 0.0 991 1.0 37 Name: provider_second, dtype: int64 ``` ::: ::: ## What fixed effects can see Subtract the provider mean and the time-invariant columns are identically zero. That is the within transformation. A slope on a column this transformation deletes is not identified. ::: {#f6f06baf .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} within_sd = sasp.groupby("id")[REGRESSORS].std().max().rename("max within-unit SD") print(within_sd.loc[TIME_INVARIANT].to_frame()) print(within_sd.loc[TIME_VARYING].to_frame()) if not np.allclose(within_sd.loc[TIME_INVARIANT], 0.0): raise RuntimeError("a listed time-invariant covariate varies within provider") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` max within-unit SD age 0.0 asq 0.0 bmi 0.0 hispanic 0.0 black 0.0 other 0.0 asian 0.0 schooling 0.0 cohab 0.0 married 0.0 divorced 0.0 separated 0.0 max within-unit SD age_cl 21.108845 unsafe 0.577350 llength 2.483792 reg 0.577350 asq_cl 2569.883301 appearance_cl 4.041452 provider_second 0.577350 asian_cl 0.577350 black_cl 0.577350 hispanic_cl 0.577350 othrace_cl 0.577350 hot 0.577350 massage_cl 0.577350 ``` ::: ::: **Takeaway:** age, BMI, race, schooling, and marital status are identified in pooled OLS and wiped by provider demeaning. The book prints them as `0.000` with a missing standard error in the FE columns. ## Bayesian within estimator This is the CausalPy result, and the comparison to Table 8.3. `fe_method="demeaned"`, time-varying formula only, `time_fe_variable` left unset, then `.fit()`. The book's pooled OLS column and provider-dummy column are cited below. They are not refit. Sampling a dummy per provider — about 257 effects — is not this page. The prior is the model's default. It is not tuned to the published numbers. `time_fe_variable` stays unset. On the demeaned path that argument is not a label: setting it also demeans by that column, which would be two-way FE. The book is one-way provider FE. Session is the within-unit index, not a second fixed effect. The demeaned formula keeps only the time-varying regressors. After demeaning, the provider characteristics are zero columns and the design is singular. Leaving them out is the result, not a shorter model. Do not add session FE, and do not drop a different set of regressors than the book does. ::: {#7e6242c1 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} demeaned_formula = "lnw ~ " + " + ".join(TIME_VARYING) rhs = demeaned_formula.split(" ~ ", 1)[1].split(" + ") if "session" in rhs or "C(session)" in demeaned_formula: raise RuntimeError("estimating formulas must not include session fixed effects") for column in TIME_INVARIANT: if column in rhs: raise RuntimeError(f"{column} is time-invariant and does not belong in the demeaned formula") sample_kwargs = { "target_accept": 0.95, "random_seed": 42, "progressbar": False, } bayes = cp.PanelRegression( sasp, demeaned_formula, unit_fe_variable="id", time_fe_variable=None, fe_method="demeaned", model=cp.pymc_models.LinearRegression(sample_kwargs=sample_kwargs), ).fit() def coefficient_means(result): """Mean coefficient by patsy label. PanelRegression keeps draws on the model backend rather than a result bundle. """ draws = result._model_backend.coefficients() return { str(name): float(draws.sel(coeffs=name).mean()) for name in draws.coords["coeffs"].values } rhat = az.rhat(bayes.idata).to_dataset() max_rhat = float(np.nanmax(rhat.to_array().values)) n_div = int(bayes.idata["sample_stats"]["diverging"].sum()) min_ess = float( np.nanmin(az.ess(bayes.idata, method="bulk").to_dataset().to_array().values) ) print(f"max r-hat {max_rhat:.4f}, divergences {n_div}, min bulk ESS {min_ess:.0f}") if bayes.time_fe_variable is not None or bayes.fe_method != "demeaned": raise RuntimeError("Bayesian fit must be one-way demeaned provider FE") bayes_means = coefficient_means(bayes) bayes.summary() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` NUTS[nutpie]: [beta, y_hat_sigma] Sampling: [y_hat] Sampling: [beta, y_hat, y_hat_sigma] ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` max r-hat 1.0091, divergences 0, min bulk ESS 467 Panel Regression ============================================================ Units: 257 (id) FE method: demeaned Observations: 1028 ============================================================ Model Coefficients: Model coefficients: Intercept -3.9e-05, 94% HDI [-0.011, 0.013] age_cl 0.0023, 94% HDI [-0.0061, 0.012] unsafe 0.051, 94% HDI [-0.002, 0.11] llength -0.43, 94% HDI [-0.46, -0.41] reg -0.037, 94% HDI [-0.07, -0.0016] asq_cl -1.5e-05, 94% HDI [-0.00011, 8.1e-05] appearance_cl 0.0056, 94% HDI [-0.003, 0.014] provider_second 0.11, 94% HDI [0.029, 0.18] asian_cl -0.011, 94% HDI [-0.072, 0.052] black_cl 0.027, 94% HDI [-0.035, 0.09] hispanic_cl -0.062, 94% HDI [-0.14, 0.017] othrace_cl 0.14, 94% HDI [0.056, 0.23] hot 0.052, 94% HDI [0.014, 0.094] massage_cl -0.0008, 94% HDI [-0.041, 0.04] ``` ::: ::: ::: {#4dd91615 .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} book_pooled = {term: targets[0] for term, targets in BOOK.items()} book_fe = {term: targets[1] for term, targets in BOOK.items()} bayes_comparison = pd.DataFrame( { "Book pooled OLS": pd.Series(book_pooled), "Book FE": pd.Series(book_fe), "Posterior mean": pd.Series({term: bayes_means[term] for term in BOOK}), } ) bayes_comparison["Posterior - book FE"] = ( bayes_comparison["Posterior mean"] - bayes_comparison["Book FE"] ) max_fe_gap = float(bayes_comparison["Posterior - book FE"].abs().max()) bayes_comparison.round(3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=7} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ::: {#cell-fig-within-slopes .cell execution_count=8} ``` {.python .cell-code} bayes.plot_coefficients(var_names=DISCUSSED) plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Posterior intervals for the within slopes the chapter discusses. These intervals are highest-density intervals, not provider-clustered standard errors.](08_panel_data_files/figure-html/fig-within-slopes-output-1.png){#fig-within-slopes width=956 height=374} ::: ::: ::: {#cell-fig-within-residuals .cell execution_count=9} ``` {.python .cell-code} bayes.plot_residuals() plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Residuals from the Bayesian within regression against fitted values.](08_panel_data_files/figure-html/fig-within-residuals-output-1.png){#fig-within-residuals width=952 height=566} ::: ::: `effect_summary()` always raises `NotImplementedError` on this class. This regression is not a difference-in-differences, interrupted time series, or synthetic-control design, and it is not `InteractiveFixedEffectsSyntheticControl`. The page does not call `effect_summary()`. `plot_unit_effects()` is dummy-FE only. This page does not fit that specification, so the method is not called. `plot_trajectories()` is not called either: it raises when `time_fe_variable` is unset, and setting that argument would change the estimator. ## Comparison to the book Removing the provider effect moves the slopes the chapter discusses. Those movements are Table 8.3's published point estimates. This page cites them. It does not refit pooled OLS or the provider-dummy column. The unsafe association is 0\.013 in the book's pooled OLS and 0\.051 with provider effects. The premium is invisible until the provider mean is removed. The Bayesian within mean is 0\.051. The session-length elasticity steepens, from \-0\.308 to \-0\.435; the posterior mean is \-0\.435. The client-attractiveness slope shrinks from 0\.020 to 0\.006 (posterior mean 0\.006), and the massage association shrinks from \-0\.134 to \-0\.001 (posterior mean \-0\.001). Time-invariant covariates drop out of the within columns. ::: {.callout-warning} A posterior highest-density interval is not a provider-clustered standard error. Table 8.3's parentheses are clustered at the provider, and they already differ slightly between the FE and demeaned columns (unsafe: 0.028 versus 0.026) even though the point estimates match. This page compares point estimates. CausalPy does not report a cluster-robust covariance here. ::: The table above compares those posterior means with Table 8.3's provider-FE point estimates. The largest absolute gap on the cited terms is 0\.001. That gap is not a clustered standard error, and the prior was not chosen to chase the printed table. | Aspect | Table 8.3 | This page | |--------|-----------|-----------| | Sample | 1,028 balanced provider-sessions | Same sample; the page stops otherwise | | Pooled OLS and provider FE | Printed to 3 decimals | Cited. Not refit | | Within estimator | Provider FE and demeaned OLS, same point estimates | Bayesian `PanelRegression`, `fe_method="demeaned"` | | Inference | Provider-clustered SEs | Posterior means and highest-density intervals. Not clustered SEs | | Session FE | Not in the estimating equation | `time_fe_variable` left unset | ## CausalPy notes Construction validates the formula and builds the design. Nothing is sampled until `.fit()`. | Fit | `fe_method` | Formula | What it is for | |-----|-------------|---------|----------------| | Bayesian within | `"demeaned"` | Time-varying regressors only | Posterior means compared with Table 8.3's published FE point estimates. Not a clustered SE | There is no hierarchical or partial-pooling fixed effect in this fit. The chapter does not ask for one. The book's pooled OLS and provider-dummy columns are not fits on this page. ## Summary Provider fixed effects and the within transformation answer the same point-estimate question, and only that question. They delete time-invariant confounding. They leave reverse causality and session-varying confounding alone. On this survey, that distinction is visible: the unsafe premium and the steeper session-length elasticity show up once the provider mean is removed, and the time-invariant covariates do not survive the transformation. --- ::: {.callout-note} ## Further reading - First edition: [Chapter 8: Panel Data](https://mixtape-1ed.netlify.app/08-panel_data) - CausalPy: [Panel fixed effects](https://causalpy.readthedocs.io/en/latest/notebooks/panel-fixed-effects.html) - Cunningham and Kendall, Survey of Adult Service Providers. Data file `sasp_panel.dta` in the [Mixtape repo](https://github.com/scunning1975/mixtape). The coded exercise uses this file; it is not a published paper. ::: ## References ::: {#refs} :::
